title: Gradient orbs

reference.note: held locally; this page carries statistics measured from it and none of its pixels

summary: Equal opaque discs stepping down a sheet, each a ramp from its rim color to a shared red that gathers in soft pools and restarts along arcs; the last disc reflects a simple room; one grain jitters the ramps.
units: reference pixels; the plate is 1199 × 1696 and every length scales with the canvas

discs.does: How many discs step down the sheet. The chain is re-spaced to fit.

radius.does: Radius of every disc. All discs are the same size, as in the source: 286 px on a 1199 px sheet.

step.does: Vertical distance between neighbors. Below 1 they overlap; the lower disc always lies on top. Measured 0.51 to 0.73 R.

wander.does: How far the chain drifts sideways as it descends. The source's centers swing 0.15 to 0.6 R between neighbors.

seed.does: Re-rolls the drift, the arcs inside each disc and the side each rim ramp is long on.

pools.does: Soft pools of the core red inside each disc. Their union, 1 − Π(1 − m), is how far a pixel moves from the rim color to the core.

base.does: Radius of one wide soft pool per disc, 0.1 to 0.3 R off center on the side opposite the long rim ramp. It keeps every rim moving toward the core from its very edge, as the source's do. 0 removes it.

poolSize.does: Radius of the pools, 0.7 to 1.3 times this. Measured: the orange disc's three pools run 0.35 to 0.6 R across.

poolSoft.does: Length of each pool's ramp as a share of its radius: m = 1 − (1 − t)^1.5. Near 1 the pool is a soft dome; small values give a flat red plate with a short edge.

spread.does: How far from the disc's center the pools may sit.

arcs.does: Offset circles about the disc's size. Each is a crease: the ramp to the core restarts from it on both sides, so where it crosses a pool a thin line of rim color cuts the red.

reach.does: Every arc is a circle 0.85 to 1.15 R across that passes through a point 0.45 R out on the disc's exposed side (away from the disc laid over it), so the creases fall where they show. This scales that 0.45 R.

crease.does: Length of the ramp on the sharp side of a crease, 0.7 to 1.3 times this. Measured: the pink disc's crease goes from rim color to full red in about 40 px on its sharp side.

rimLen.does: Length of the ramp in from each disc's edge, 0.35 to 0.85 longer on one side of the disc than the other.

core.does: How fully the ramps reach the shared core red. 0 leaves flat rim-colored discs.

highlight.does: Strength of the pale highlight on the last disc.

hiSize.does: How high into the reflected sky the pale band reaches: it runs from just above the horizon up to 0.4 plus this in elevation, fading over its top 0.5. At 0.4 it ends under the cool spot, as in the source.

shade.does: The near-black shade on the last disc: a terminator band at 0.7 R plus a flat blob under the highlight, fitted to the source with rmse 0.07.

spot.does: How far down the reflected sky the cool zenith color reaches: at 0.9 it begins 0.8 up in elevation, an ellipse about 0.66 by 0.28 R at the top of the last disc, as measured.

edge.does: Width of the disc edge. Measured 1 to 2 px: the discs are cut, not blurred.

glass.does: Lets a disc multiply with what lies beneath it. Measured 0: the source discs are opaque.

jitter.does: σ of the grain-field offset each pixel reads its ramp at. It puts the grain where the ramp is steep: high-pass σ about 1.1 in the mint-to-red mix, 0.4 in the flat red.

grain.does: Luminance grain screened over every tone by the same field. Measured 0.3 on the ground.

phase.does: Position along the loop. Turns every arc, every rim ramp and the light around its disc by one revolution; the grain boils as it goes.

modes.saw: value up to value + amp over period seconds, then again
modes.drift: seeded walk, one step of up to amp every period seconds, folded back at the slider ends

motion.runs: only while Motion is on, at half scale; the sliders hold the center values; off by default

live.runs: only while Live is on: a drag on the figure sets x across and y down between these ends; off by default

techniques.name: Edge
techniques.implementation: Cut edge: the disc color meets the ground in 1.5 px with no halo.

techniques.name: Pull
techniques.implementation: Crease: an arc where the ramp starts over, rim color on the line, red reached in about 30 px on its sharp side.

techniques.name: Grain
techniques.implementation: Mix: halfway along the ramp the mint and the red average to a dusty rose; the grain is densest here.

techniques.name: Light
techniques.implementation: Pale band: the reflected sky from 0.24 below the horizon to 0.9 up, fading over its bottom 0.4, brightest left of center.

pass_order: chain: equal discs stepped down the sheet with a seeded sideways swing; each later disc lies on top
one grain field: position-hashed noise softened 2.2 px and normalized to σ 1; it jitters the distance the pools are read at and screens every tone

per disc and per pixel: the union of four soft pools and one wide base pool, 1 − Π(1 − m), each pool m = 1 − (1 − t)^1.5; times the same ramp restarted from every arc (short on one side, three times longer on the other) and from the disc's own edge; color = rim color moved toward the core red by that amount

the last disc only: a glossy sphere reflecting one simple room along each pixel's reflected ray: a pale band from 0.24 below the horizon to 0.9 up, a cool zenith, a dark floor, the base color at grazing angles
composite in order with a 1.5 px anti-aliased cut edge; Glass, at 0 by default, multiplies a disc with what lies beneath
the grain field screens the whole sheet at σ 0.5

measured.disc_radius_evidence: Hough circles on the Lab gradient; all six radii 284 to 288
measured.blend_rule: opaque: a rim 6 px inside the mint disc reads (175,210,176) over pink and (172,209,180) over ground
measured.ramp_profile: hard crease then (1 − d/L)^1.5: L 76 px on the mint disc's soft side; about 25 px on a crease's sharp side

rim_width_by_angle.mint_disc: red reached 19 to 24 px in from the edge at −30 to −10 degrees, 51 to 145 px or never elsewhere
rim_width_by_angle.method: L < 120 along 15 radii from the fitted center

lit_disc.order_top_to_bottom: red rim, cool spot at 0.64 R up, red, pale band from 0.35 R up to 0.1 R down, red, dark floor, red rim 0.15 to 0.2 R wide
lit_disc.method: crops at 1 and 2 times, row means through the center

grain_hp_sigma.method: L minus a 2 px gaussian; it is largest where the ramp is steepest, the mark of a ramp read at a jittered position

benchmark.computed: live, when this page loads, by the code that measured the reference: default parameters, Pink red palette, 1× reference size

setup.note: The chain is generated, so each disc patch sits at the same offset from the matching disc's center as in the source: the olive disc's top pool (search.py agreed within 8 px), the mint disc's upper right edge, the first disc's left edge over the ground, the lit disc's highlight.

limits: Bench mean 0.962, lowest 0.77 (rim ramp histogram). The chain and its pools are generated, so four disc patches are matched by place in the matching disc, not by pixel. The rim ramp patch scores 0.77 to 0.93 on its histogram and contrast: the source's mint disc has one narrow rim where a red pool runs to within 20 px of the edge, and the generated mint disc reaches red 44 to 64 px in; the nearest honest spot was used.
The lit disc is a reflection model, not the source's hand-placed blobs: its highlight patch scores 0.89 on histogram and contrast because the source's pale band is wider at its center.

The source's ground is a warm light gray (240, 235, 229); every palette here, the measured one included, uses a neutral ground of the same lightness (236, 236, 235). That costs the ground color metric about 0.01.
The source is a JPEG whose 8 px blocks soften its grain: the render's grain is softened 2.2 px to meet the ground spectrum at 0.95.
notes: Deterministic: the same palette, parameters and seed give the same pixels.
A display render is capped at 2.4 megapixels; a slider in motion draws at half scale (down to a quarter on a heavy engine) and the release redraws in full.
This spec follows the controls: open it again, or leave it open, after changing them.
